submission:
Root cause: Two minutes before onset, platform-automation rewrote the frontend pod spec's DNS settings: it removed the cluster-default `dnsPolicy: ClusterFirst` and substituted an explicit `dnsConfig` pointing at a single public resolver (8.8.8.8) [tr_929c50e7f8bf]. A public resolver cannot answer for cluster-internal service names, so frontend can neither resolve nor reach any in-cluster dependency, and the value named in that config is itself the thing that breaks every request. The downstream picture is consistent: frontend produced no spans of any kind, inbound or outbound, across the whole window [tr_2dcc48fc8659] and no log lines at all [tr_66fc0c934048], while frontend-proxy — the caller that alerted — shows an error ratio near 0.905 with intervals where its call volume disappears entirely [tr_2635c8e1c2ef]. frontend-proxy is the service that noticed, not the service that failed; its Envoy restarted cleanly at ~08:48:51 with no fatal startup output [tr_362c05685e3e], so the proxy binary and bootstrap are not the defect. The failing mechanism is a configuration value that names the wrong resolver.
Faulty component: frontend
Fault type: bad_config
Confidence: medium

Evidence:
- Four changes landed on frontend, all authored by platform-automation and all clustered within ~3 minutes before onset rather than spread over hours. (found, from change_history on frontend)
- The two most recent changes, applied simultaneously ~2 minutes before onset, altered the pod's DNS resolution behaviour: the cluster-default DNS policy was removed and replaced by an explicit custom DNS configuration pointing at a single public resolver. (found, from change_history on frontend)
- The workload itself was created only ~3 minutes before onset, alongside creation of the frontend Service object — this is a fresh bring-up, not a mutation of a long-running stable deployment. (found, from change_history on frontend)
- A DNS configuration that bypasses the in-cluster resolver would prevent resolution of cluster-internal service names, making this the strongest candidate cause among the four changes. (found, from change_history on frontend)
- An application code deploy or container image version bump triggered the incident. (ruled_out, from change_history on frontend; why: No image or version change appears in the change set; the only mutations are DNS-related pod spec fields, plus creation events.)
- A feature-flag toggle flipped behaviour just before onset. (ruled_out, from change_history on frontend; why: No feature-flag updates are recorded for frontend in the window.)
- A human operator made a manual or ad-hoc change. (ruled_out, from change_history on frontend; why: All four changes are attributed to the same automation actor, not an individual.)
- The trigger was a slow-building change landed hours earlier that only manifested at onset. (ruled_out, from change_history on frontend; why: The change history over the queried window contains nothing earlier than ~3 minutes before onset; every recorded change is tightly adjacent to it.)
- A routing/Service definition change broke traffic reaching frontend. (ruled_out, from change_history on frontend; why: The Service was created, not modified, and it predates the DNS mutations; no subsequent routing edits are recorded.)
- The error-ratio template returned a single defined sample in the incident window at roughly 0.905, i.e. about nine in ten frontend-proxy spans carried an error status at that point. (found, from metric_baseline on frontend-proxy; query: sum by(service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend-proxy",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])) / sum by(service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend-proxy"}[5m])))
- Three intervals in the incident window produced no defined ratio at all. For a ratio built on call-rate denominators this means no spans were recorded in those intervals — frontend-proxy traffic went absent, not merely erroring. (found, from metric_baseline on frontend-proxy; query: sum by(service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend-proxy",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])) / sum by(service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend-proxy"}[5m])))
- The 30-minute baseline window immediately before the incident contains no samples whatsoever, so there is no pre-incident error level to compare against; the reported move from 0 to 0.905 is an artifact of an empty baseline rather than a measured rise. (found, from metric_baseline on frontend-proxy; query: sum by(service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend-proxy",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])) / sum by(service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend-proxy"}[5m])))
- The tool's own verdict is that it found no sustained departure from baseline, which given the single incident sample and empty baseline should be read as insufficient data rather than as evidence of stability. (found, from metric_baseline on frontend-proxy; query: sum by(service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend-proxy",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])) / sum by(service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend-proxy"}[5m])))
- The question's other two quantities are unanswered: this result carries only a span-derived error ratio, with no request-rate counter, no HTTP status breakdown separating 5xx from 503, and no upstream connection-failure metric. (found, from metric_baseline on frontend-proxy; query: sum by(service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend-proxy",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])) / sum by(service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend-proxy"}[5m])))
- frontend-proxy was serving traffic normally and the fault lies entirely downstream (ruled_out, from metric_baseline on frontend-proxy; why: The one defined sample puts the error ratio near 0.905, so frontend-proxy itself is emitting overwhelmingly error-status spans; it is not a healthy pass-through during this window.; query: sum by(service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend-proxy",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])) / sum by(service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend-proxy"}[5m])))
- This is a slow degradation that had been building through the preceding half hour (ruled_out, from metric_baseline on frontend-proxy; why: The baseline half-hour produced zero samples, so no gradual ramp is visible there. Whatever happened is not a trend this data captured; the series begins in the incident window.; query: sum by(service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend-proxy",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])) / sum by(service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend-proxy"}[5m])))
- Errors are elevated but request volume held steady, pointing at a per-request failure mode rather than a collapse (ruled_out, from metric_baseline on frontend-proxy; why: Three incident-window intervals have no defined ratio, which for this query means an empty denominator — no calls recorded. Volume did not hold steady; it dropped out entirely for part of the window.; query: sum by(service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend-proxy",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])) / sum by(service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend-proxy"}[5m])))
- The error ratio is a stable long-running condition that predates the incident (ruled_out, from metric_baseline on frontend-proxy; why: The template reports the baseline as exactly zero with no samples, so there is no evidence of a standing error floor; the condition cannot be shown to predate the window.; query: sum by(service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend-proxy",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])) / sum by(service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend-proxy"}[5m])))
- A trace query for the frontend service over the full ~30-minute incident window returned no spans at all — neither inbound (frontend as server) nor outbound (frontend as client). (found, from trace_query on frontend)
- Because no outbound spans exist, there is no trace-level evidence of name-resolution or connection errors from frontend to cluster-internal services; the question cannot be answered affirmatively from traces. (found, from trace_query on frontend)
- The total absence (rather than a reduced volume or a wall of error spans) is consistent with either frontend not executing any instrumented request handling during the window, or frontend telemetry not reaching the trace backend at all. (found, from trace_query on frontend)
- frontend is up and serving traffic but its outbound calls are failing with DNS/name-resolution errors to cluster-internal services (ruled_out, from trace_query on frontend; why: That failure mode produces outbound client spans carrying error status. Zero spans of any kind were recorded, so this pattern is not present in trace data.)
- frontend is partially degraded — some requests succeeding, some failing — i.e. an elevated error rate rather than a total stop (ruled_out, from trace_query on frontend; why: Partial degradation still emits successful spans alongside failing ones. The window contains no spans at all, so a mixed success/failure profile is excluded.)
- A slow or timing-out downstream dependency is the proximate cause, visible as long-duration frontend client spans (ruled_out, from trace_query on frontend; why: Timeouts and latency still generate spans with long durations. No spans were emitted, so this cannot be the trace-visible cause.)
- frontend is receiving requests from upstream callers during the incident (ruled_out, from trace_query on frontend; why: Inbound server spans would appear for frontend if callers were reaching it. None exist, so either no traffic arrived or frontend never recorded it.)
- A Loki query for frontend pods in the astronomy-shop namespace returned no matching log lines across the full ~30 minute incident window, so line volume is zero, not non-zero. (found, from logql_query on frontend; query: {namespace="astronomy-shop",pod=~"frontend-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- The zero-line result is consistent with the service's described normal silence; nothing in this result distinguishes genuine application silence from a log-collection or pod-label-matching gap, and the result carries a truncation flag that weakens it further. (found, from logql_query on frontend; query: {namespace="astronomy-shop",pod=~"frontend-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- frontend emitted an error burst, panic, or stack-trace spike during the incident that would identify it as the origin (ruled_out, from logql_query on frontend; why: No lines of any level were returned for frontend pods over the entire window, so no logged burst exists in this index to support that story.; query: {namespace="astronomy-shop",pod=~"frontend-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- Frontend log volume can be used as a correlating signal (a rise or fall timed to the incident) for timeline construction (ruled_out, from logql_query on frontend; why: Volume is flat at zero for the whole window, so there is no variation to correlate against; this line of investigation is closed and the timeline must be built from metrics, traces, or upstream services.; query: {namespace="astronomy-shop",pod=~"frontend-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- The incident can be diagnosed from frontend logs alone (ruled_out, from logql_query on frontend; why: The service produced no retrievable log evidence, so log-only diagnosis is not available here regardless of frontend's actual involvement.; query: {namespace="astronomy-shop",pod=~"frontend-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- The only frontend-proxy log lines returned in the 30-minute window are Envoy server startup output — the extension/plugin registry dump emitted during server initialization — all timestamped at a single moment near the end of the window (~08:48:51). (found, from logql_query on frontend-proxy; query: {namespace="astronomy-shop",pod=~"frontend-proxy-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- Envoy in the frontend-proxy pod (re)started at approximately 08:48:51, roughly three minutes before the window closes, indicating a container start or restart late in the incident rather than a steadily running proxy. (found, from logql_query on frontend-proxy; query: {namespace="astronomy-shop",pod=~"frontend-proxy-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- Startup proceeded normally to the point of enumerating all compiled-in extensions at info level, with no error- or critical-level lines in the returned output, so the process did not abort during early initialization. (found, from logql_query on frontend-proxy; query: {namespace="astronomy-shop",pod=~"frontend-proxy-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- No access-log entries, no response-flag records (e.g. upstream connect/reset or no-healthy-upstream markers), no DNS/resolution failures, and no 503-toward-frontend-upstream evidence appear anywhere in the returned data; the question's core ask is unanswered by this result. (found, from logql_query on frontend-proxy; query: {namespace="astronomy-shop",pod=~"frontend-proxy-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- frontend-proxy ran continuously through the incident and the fault lies purely downstream of it (ruled_out, from logql_query on frontend-proxy; why: The result captures a fresh Envoy initialization sequence inside the window, so the proxy process itself was replaced or restarted during the incident. Any theory assuming an uninterrupted proxy lifetime is closed.; query: {namespace="astronomy-shop",pod=~"frontend-proxy-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- Envoy is stuck in a crash-loop caused by a bad bootstrap/config that prevents the server from coming up (ruled_out, from logql_query on frontend-proxy; why: The startup sequence advances all the way through the full extension-registry dump at info level with no fatal output, which is well past the point where a malformed bootstrap would abort.; query: {namespace="astronomy-shop",pod=~"frontend-proxy-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- The absence of proxy logs is due to the pod being unscheduled, terminated, or having no log stream at all for the window (ruled_out, from logql_query on frontend-proxy; why: The pod selector matched and returned real stdout content, so the pod exists, is emitting logs, and Loki is ingesting from it. The gap is a content gap, not a collection gap.; query: {namespace="astronomy-shop",pod=~"frontend-proxy-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- Access logging is disabled or unsupported in this Envoy build, explaining why no request records appear (ruled_out, from logql_query on frontend-proxy; why: The startup dump explicitly registers the file/stdout/stderr access-logger extensions, so access-log capability is present in the binary; their absence must be explained some other way.; query: {namespace="astronomy-shop",pod=~"frontend-proxy-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- The error-ratio metric query for frontend returned no data at all over the 30-minute incident window, and the backend reported the failure explicitly: the span-derived metrics this template reads are not present for this service because it emits no traces that are converted into metrics. (found, from metric_baseline on frontend)
- No request rate, error rate, latency, or saturation (CPU/memory/restart) values for frontend were obtained from this result — the query failed before returning any series, so all four requested signals remain unmeasured by this tool call. (found, from metric_baseline on frontend)
- The comparison baseline window (07:51–08:21) is equally unpopulated, so no before/after delta can be computed from this source. (found, from metric_baseline on frontend)
- The empty result means frontend's error rate is zero and the service is healthy — frontend can be cleared as a suspect. (ruled_out, from metric_baseline on frontend; why: The result carries an explicit failure reason distinguishing unavailable from zero: the underlying series do not exist for this service. An absent series is not a measurement of zero, so health cannot be inferred either way.)
- Frontend's RED signals can be retrieved from span-derived metrics in this Prometheus instance, so further span-metric queries against frontend will resolve the question. (ruled_out, from metric_baseline on frontend; why: The backend states frontend produces no traces that become metrics, so this entire query family is a dead end for this service; the investigation must pivot to non-span sources (kubelet/cAdvisor for CPU, memory and restarts, ingress or proxy counters for request and error counts, or raw logs).)
- A gap or drop in frontend's error-ratio chart starting around the incident time is itself evidence of an outage or scrape failure caused by the incident. (ruled_out, from metric_baseline on frontend; why: The absence extends across both the incident window and the preceding baseline window, so it is a structural property of the instrumentation rather than something that changed at 08:51:43.)

Reasoning:
The change record is the only concrete, timed act in the window and it is tightly adjacent to onset (~2 minutes) [tr_929c50e7f8bf]; the same record rules out an image/version bump and any feature-flag toggle, which removes bad_deploy and feature_flag as competing stories for how this started. What makes this bad_config rather than merely a config edit upstream of something else is that the wrong value *is* the mechanism: a pod whose only nameserver is a public resolver cannot resolve cluster-internal names, so each request fails at resolution rather than running slow, running out of a resource, or reading corrupt data. The caller-side signals follow from that: frontend-proxy emits overwhelmingly error-status spans and loses call volume for part of the window [tr_2635c8e1c2ef], which is what a proxy does when its upstream is unreachable. The specialists explicitly declined to treat frontend's empty metric and trace results as proof of health — the metric series are structurally absent for frontend in this Prometheus, in baseline as well as incident window [tr_a9a3db832182], and the trace absence is noted as ambiguous between 'not handling requests' and 'telemetry not arriving' [tr_2dcc48fc8659]. So frontend's silence neither confirms nor refutes; it is the change record plus the caller's error profile that carry the verdict, which is why confidence is medium rather than high. I did not choose network_partition because that class expects the cut-off service's own log to complain it cannot reach anything, and frontend logged nothing at all [tr_66fc0c934048]; more importantly the cut is not a network event but a named wrong address in the pod spec.

Alternatives considered:
1. frontend: The frontend workload was created ~3 minutes before onset and never came up correctly, so there was simply no backend behind frontend-proxy during the window. (bad_deploy). Ranked lower because: The change set contains no image or version mutation at all — only DNS pod-spec fields plus creation events [tr_929c50e7f8bf] — so there is no wrong artifact to point at. Frontend's total telemetry silence is equally consistent with a pod that is up but unable to resolve anything, and the metric absence is structural rather than incident-onset [tr_a9a3db832182]. It stays plausible only because pod readiness was never directly checked.
2. frontend: frontend is running but severed from in-cluster connectivity, leaving frontend-proxy's calls to fail with no reachable upstream. (network_partition). Ranked lower because: A partitioned service normally logs that it cannot reach anything; frontend logged nothing whatsoever [tr_66fc0c934048]. And the isolation here has a named, recorded cause in a configuration value — a resolver address — rather than a network-layer event [tr_929c50e7f8bf], which makes config_revert the fix rather than restoring connectivity.

Open questions:
- No direct confirmation that frontend is actually Running and Ready — pod status, restart counts and container exit reasons were never queried, so a fresh workload that simply failed to come up cannot be excluded.
- No DNS-failure evidence was observed anywhere: frontend emitted no outbound spans [tr_2dcc48fc8659] and frontend-proxy returned no access logs or response-flag records such as no_healthy_upstream or upstream connect failure [tr_362c05685e3e], so the resolution-failure mechanism is inferred from the change record rather than witnessed.
- Whether the Envoy (re)start at ~08:48:51 [tr_362c05685e3e] is a consequence of the rollout, an unrelated bring-up, or a contributor to the error ratio is unresolved; it lands between the DNS edit and onset.
- The two earlier changes in the set (#3 and #4) were truncated in the sample and were never examined on their own merits.
- Triage reported one unmeasured edge crossed; the service on the far side of it was never dispatched against, so a dependency below frontend remains unchecked.
- frontend-proxy's HTTP status breakdown (5xx vs 503) and upstream connection-failure counters were never retrieved [tr_2635c8e1c2ef], so the caller-side failure shape is only partly characterised.
